title: AI from research question to publication
source: Brady Lund, Manika Lamba & Sang Hoo Oh · arXiv preprint · 2024

cues.text: An academic paper passes through many hands. Where can artificial intelligence speed that work up?
The authors trace these possibilities in a twenty twenty-four preprint.
At the research stage, a language model can suggest questions, search terms, or ways to approach unfamiliar literature.
Open the original sources before trusting a summary or citing a claim.
AI can help write code or organize an analysis. Check the code, the data, and every result used in your argument.
The researcher still chooses the method and interprets the findings.
Writing tools can suggest a structure, revise wording, or help a draft read more clearly.
Verify quotations and citations yourself. Follow the journal's policy for disclosing how you used the tool.
Editorial systems can assist with technical screening or organizing submissions.
Expert reviewers still judge the research question, the soundness of the method, and what the work contributes.
Keep confidential material within the permitted workflow.
The preprint describes where AI might assist and where journals would need rules. Its policy examples come from twenty twenty-four.
At every stage, people remain responsible for the claims, the evidence, and the decisions.
